paragraphs: Here's what gets me, friend. Habakkuk doesn't dress his prayer up. He says, "How long, O LORD, must I call for help but You do not hear…" (Habakkuk 1:2), and the LORD doesn't scold him for it. Habakkuk brings the hard, honest stuff straight to God, and God answers him. So when you've got questions, take them to the LORD too.

Now, the answer Habakkuk gets is NOT the one he ordered. The LORD says He is doing a work that Habakkuk "would never believe even if someone told" him (Habakkuk 1:5), and then He names the Chaldeans (Habakkuk 1:6). It's like you ask for one thing and the answer shows up in a box you didn't even know existed. I think Habakkuk is sitting there with his mouth open. God's ways are bigger than what we can see from where we stand.

Look at the end of it, friend. The Chaldeans look unstoppable, laughing at fortresses and sweeping by like the wind. But the LORD says, "They are guilty; their own strength is their god" (Habakkuk 1:11). Power that answers to nobody is not the last word. And the story isn't over, because Habakkuk still has more to say.
